To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) we study the sequential learning of new categories in GANs, (b) we show that sequential fine-tuning causes the model to forget previous categories, (c) we propose a memory replay generator that can mitigate this forgetting, and (d) we show that this method can generate competitive images from the new categories, while significantly improving the generation quality from previous categories.

(1) we propose Memory Replay Generative Adversarial Networks (MeRGAN), a conditional generative adversarial framework that integrates a generator with a memory replay; (2) we show that MeRGAN can generate images that are competitive with those generated by a GAN trained on the same dataset; and (3) we show that our method can significantly mitigate the forgetting of previous classes when training a GAN on a sequential fashion.
we present a novel approach to prevent forgetting in GANs by integrating a memory replay generator that is jointly trained with the main network.
